name: Miami Modernism
summary: A regional style of modern architecture in Miami that evolved from Art Deco.
description: It features bold geometric forms, glass walls, and tropical adaptations with a playful spirit. This style emerged in post-war Miami as a more progressive interpretation of modernism while retaining decorative elements from the earlier Art Deco period.
culturalContext: MiMo (Miami Modernism, 1950s-1966) — Miami Beach's postwar answer to Art Deco — dressed resort hotels in relief-screen walls (biscayne breeze blocks), cantilevered porte-cocheres, boomerang balconies, nautical motifs and neon-sculpted signage: the Fontainebleau (Morris Lapidus, 1954), Eden Roc and the di Lido strip. Designed for drive-in tourism and air-conditioned glamour, it fell to redevelopment before preservationists (MiMo Biscayne Association) won districts on Biscayne Boulevard and Collins Waterfront.
